synthesis.body: Adding a test suite to a Windows/macOS parity runner only exercises what its assertions actually run. A test guarded by `skipif(os.name != 'posix')` skips on the very runner it was added for, so the platform-specific arm stays unverified while a green run is read as verifying it — worse than no test, because it retires the 'named limitation' caveat without earning it. Write the assertion cross-platform where you can (spawn a grandchild via subprocess.Popen rather than os.fork; probe liveness via os.kill(pid, 0) on POSIX and tasklist on Windows), or state in the AC that the arm remains unverified.

title: A platform-skipped assertion inside a cross-platform parity suite reads as coverage and proves nothing
